title: Rate limits + org/project keys demo with CareSync Health
meeting_header: Date: 2025-06-17 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 52m\nAttendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Arjun Mehta (Redwood CSM); Priya Patel (CareSync), Tom Reynolds (CareSync), Jasmine Lee (CareSync), Ben Wu (CareSync SRE)
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of rate limits, quotas, and org/project keys in the Console and API. Focus on multi-tenant controls, per-project quotas, org-level defaults, and key rotation. Customer raised questions about per-tenant isolation, SOC2 controls, and how quotas affect routing/fallbacks. Agreed next steps: send security pack, pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot, and set up a short POC account to run benchmark tests.
action_items: Lena Park: send security & SOC2 pack + link to compliance docs by 2025-06-19
Miguel Santos: share step-by-step demo recording and screenshots of rate-limit config by 2025-06-18
Arjun Mehta: create trial org + project in Redwood Console for CareSync by 2025-06-20
next_steps: Redwood to share security deck and SOC2 report
Schedule 1-week pilot: Redwood will provision trial org and preconfigure per-project quotas
Customer to run small benchmark with 2-3 routes and share perf targets
Follow-up call to review pilot results week of 2025-06-30
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - I'm Lena, AE on the account, and Miguel is our SE. We figure 45-ish minutes for a live demo focused on rate limits, quotas and how org/project keys work in the Console.

[00:18] Miguel (Redwood SE): Hi, Miguel here. I'll jump into the Console and show a few examples - forgive any typos, sometimes the auto-transcript gets Redwood Ded.. Dedic8 wrong.

[00:30] Priya (CareSync): Thanks. We're mainly interested in multi-tenant controls - each of our clinics needs a separate quota and we need to throttle per-route for high-cost generation routes. Also security questions later.

[00:45] Tom (CareSync): We have strict SSO and KMS requirements; also we want rate limits to prevent noisy tenants from hurting others.

[00:58] Miguel: Great. Opening the Console - top left you can see Org settings. We support org-wide defaults and then project-level overrides. I'll create a demo project called 'clinic-alpha' and show how to attach keys and limits.

[01:25] [screen share noise] Miguel: So under Projects, click New Project, name it. Here you can create Project API keys - these are scoped to the project. We also have Org keys for cross-project access and Project keys for strict isolation.

[01:50] Jasmine (CareSync): How are keys rotated and audited? We need to show auditors logs.

[01:55] Miguel: Keys can be rotated in the UI or via the API; rotation event shows up in Audit Logs. We retain detailed logs for configured retention (notes: enterprise plan has extended retention). We also integrate with customer KMS for private deployments.

[02:20] Miguel: Now rate limits. You can set per-project QPS and token-per-minute limits. There's also per-route limits - so you could throttle the /generate-text endpoint more strictly than /embeddings.

[02:42] Priya: Token-based metering is good. Does the UI expose estimated costs when changing quotas?

[02:50] Miguel: We show a cost impact estimate based on your historical usage profile if available - it'll say, approximate monthly cost delta. It's an estimate, helpful for guardrails.

[03:10] Ben (CareSync SRE): Suppose a tenant exceeds their quota. What's the behavior? Do we queue, reject, or route to a lower-cost model?

[03:20] Miguel: By default, requests above quota get HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. You can configure fallback policies to route to a cheaper model or to set a soft quota which returns warnings in the response headers while still allowing limited traffic. We can also burst for short windows if you allow bursting in the project policy.

[03:49] Lena: Important for reliability - our platform supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants, which keeps apps online.

[04:10] Tom: On Dedicated vs Hosted - if we go Dedicated, does rate limiting happen in your control plane or ours? We need data isolation.

[04:22] Miguel: For Dedicated we run isolated GPU pools for you; control plane can be Private, and Audit + keys live in your VPC if you choose Private deployment. The rate limiting enforcement can be colocated in your VPC for extra isolation.

[04:40] Jasmine: SOC2 and encryption questions - where are keys stored? Is there HSM support?

[04:48] Miguel: Keys are encrypted at rest; for Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM. SOC2 Type II report is available - we'll include it in the security pack.

[05:05] [00:05 lag] Miguel: Now demo: creating a per-route rate limit. Click into the project's Rate Limits tab, Add Rule. I'll set route = /v1/generate, limit = 20 requests per minute, token limit = 50k tokens per hour, and assign alert thresholds at 80%. Save.

[05:40] Miguel: You can combine rules by tag, by route, or by API key. If you use per-key enforcement we can show which customer key tripped the limit in the logs.

[06:00] Priya: We have a lot of short-chat requests and occasional long generations. Can we set a token cap per-request and per-day quotas?

[06:12] Miguel: Yes - there's a per-request token cap and a rolling 24-hour or calendar quota. We also support soft quotas with webhooks so you can be notified before hard enforcement kicks in.

[06:30] [06:30] Miguel: Let me show the API call example. This is REST: POST /v1/generate with header x-redwood-project-key: <key>. If a key is scoped to a project the enforcement is straightforward; org keys can be used across projects but the org-level default limits apply unless overridden.

[06:55] Tom: Are project keys JWTs or opaque keys? We have rotation automation that works with JWTs preferably.

[07:05] Miguel: They are opaque API keys today, but we support short-lived tokens via the Token Exchange API - you can mint short-lived tokens with your ID provider. That's in our private deployment docs.

[07:25] Priya: How does this interact with billing? If we set quotas, do we still get billed for anything beyond?

[07:32] Lena: Quotas are a protective control; billing is usage-based. If you exceed quota but allow bursting, you'll be billed for the extra usage. We'll map quotas to cost centers in the billing UI for multi-tenant chargebacks.

[07:55] Ben: Any rate limit enforcement latency? We don't want enforcement checks to add p99 latency to generation calls.

[08:05] Miguel: Enforcement is in-path but optimized - we use local caches for counts and only occasionally sync to central counters. P99 impact should be negligible (single-digit ms), but we'll include numbers in the benchmarking doc.

[08:22] [screen noise] Miguel: Showing Audit Logs - you can filter by API key, project, and event type (request, key-rotation, quota-change). Exports are CSV/JSON.

[08:45] Jasmine: For auditors we need proof of RBAC changes and who changed a quota.

[08:50] Miguel: That's in audit logs with user identity - SAML integrations populate the user email. We also sign important events.

[09:05] Priya: Demo the Optimize recommendations - can Redwood suggest batching or quantization to lower cost per token?

[09:15] Miguel: Yes, Redwood Optimize suggests batching windows per workload, cache TTLs for prefix caching, and quantization levels per model. You can apply suggestions programmatically or via Console.

[09:35] Priya: If we set aggressive batching, how does that impact latency? Some routes are real-time.

[09:45] Miguel: You can define route-level SLOs. The optimizer won't recommend batching for routes with strict latency SLOs. It gives tradeoff metrics - latency vs tokens saved.

[10:05] Lena: Quick interruption - any regulatory constraints we should be aware of for US clinics?

[10:12] Jasmine: Data residency and PHI handling. We may need an on-prem or isolated VPC for PHI.

[10:22] Miguel: For PHI we recommend Private deployment with your KMS and configured retention; we also support on-prem package. We'll include the compliance checklist.

[10:40] Miguel: Back to rate limits - showing rule history: you'll see hits, breached events, and top offending keys. You can set automatic throttles or manual review.

[11:02] Tom: Can we have different quotas for different environments (prod vs stage) under the same org?

[11:08] Miguel: Yes - projects map well to environments; you can also tag keys with env:prod and apply rules by tag.

[11:25] Priya: For the POC, we'd like a sample config: 3 projects (alpha, beta, shared) with per-project keys, per-route limits, and a cheap model fallback.

[11:35] Miguel: We can pre-provision that. I'll also add webhook integrations for quota alerts to your PagerDuty.

[11:50] [minor crosstalk] Lena: Let's talk about pricing briefly - reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go.

[11:58] Lena: Dedicated offers predictable throughput; reserved commits lower unit cost. Hosted is faster to start. We'll send a side-by-side for cost per 1M tokens and tail latency targets.

[12:20] Priya: Any customer references with similar multi-tenant constraints?

[12:26] Lena: We can share anonymized case studies; we'll include a short reference list in the follow-ups.

[12:40] Miguel: Demo end-to-end example: an incoming request from clinic app with project key X hits the gateway, enforcement checks local counters; if below quota it proceeds to serving runtime; if over quota the fallback to cheaper model is attempted, otherwise 429 is returned.

[13:05] Ben: Can we throttle by token budget rather than requests? Some calls are small, some massive.

[13:12] Miguel: Yes, token budgets are first-class rules. You can set per-project token budgets per hour/day/month.

[13:30] [13:30] Miguel: I'm going to run a quick simulated breach so you can see logs - triggering a synthetic spike.

[13:45] [simulation noise] Miguel: Logs show the key and route, count of requests, and alert firing at 80%. You can click to open the incident and toggle an auto-remediate which will reduce the rate limit by 50% for 10 minutes.

[14:05] Jasmine: Is auto-remediate safe? We don't want accidental throttling during maintenance windows.

[14:12] Miguel: There are guardrails - only admins can enable auto-remediate and there's an approval flow. Also maintenance windows can be set.

[14:30] Priya: On observability, do we get token-level cost breakouts?

[14:36] Miguel: Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route and per-key. You can also export to your billing system or S3.

[14:55] Tom: Anything else about network egress or region affinity? We need low latency from APAC clinics.

[15:04] Miguel: We support regional routing policies; you can pin projects to regions and we have multi-region fallbacks.

[15:20] Lena: Ok let's recap and confirm next steps. Miguel will share the recording and sample config. I'll send pricing + security pack. Arjun will spin up a trial org. CareSync will run a small benchmark and share targets.

[15:40] Priya: Sounds good. Timeline - we'd like the trial by next week.

[15:46] Lena: We'll aim for that. Anything else?

[15:51] Ben: One more question - can we map quotas to internal cost centers for chargeback?

[15:55] Lena: Yes, billing tags and project mapping support chargebacks. We'll show an example on the billing page.

[16:05] Tom: Thanks everyone.

[16:10] Miguel: Thanks - we'll follow up with docs and a trial org.

[16:15] [end of recording]
